hints.title: Monthly Order Aggregation Filtering
hints.text: Filter orders placed in February 2020, sum units by product, and retain products with total units >= 100.

hints.title: Having Filter on Summed Units
hints.text: join Products with Orders, filter on order_date between 2020-02-01 and 2020-02-29, and use having sum(unit) >= 100.

hints.title: Product Orders Blueprint
hints.text: select p.product_name, sum(o.unit) as unit from Products p join Orders o on p.product_id = o.product_id where o.order_date between "2020-02-01" and "2020-02-29" group by p.product_id, p.product_name having sum(o.unit) >= 100.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT p.product_name, SUM(o.unit) AS unit
FROM Products p
JOIN Orders o ON p.product_id = o.product_id
WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN '2020-02-01' AND '2020-02-29'
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name
HAVING SUM(o.unit) >= 100;
```

complexity.notes: Date filtering followed by group aggregation runs in linear time relative to monthly orders.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Grouping without date restrictions tallies units across the entire order history.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: HAVING clause prunes low-volume products prior to output materialization.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Date filtering for February 2020 leap year and HAVING sum >= 100.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def list_products(products: pd.DataFrame, orders: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    feb = orders[orders['order_date'].astype(str).str.startswith('2020-02')]
    merged = feb.merge(products, on='product_id')
    grouped = merged.groupby(['product_name'])['unit'].sum().reset_index()
    return grouped[grouped['unit'] >= 100]
solutions.approach: Pandas Date String Filter and Groupby Sum
